Hub meta-leader on T4

Hub leadership can be requested, but regional recovery can disturb it. Metadata quorum and stream availability remain separate.

Every number on this page comes from a kept run. The words never state a number — they point at a check ID. Expected is the design. Measured is what the machine did.

Findings

Hub leadership can be requested

A step-down with --cluster arb put the meta leader in the hub in every trial. Start-up does not put it there: nothing in the config pins it.

Evidence: ML26, ML36, ML41, ML93, ML111, ML5a

A dark region does not move a hub leader

With the leader in the hub, one dark region left six voters, above the quorum. The leader held, the term did not move, and metadata and writes went on.

Evidence: ML44, ML61, ML49a, ML66a

Regional recovery can disturb it

Recovery always came back. Leadership did not always stay put: on a return the leader sometimes moved out of the hub — in some rounds to the region that stayed up, in others to the returning region — and sometimes the same server came back in a higher term. The cause is not proved. Read the cross-run table before quoting a rate: the rounds are few.

Evidence: ML54, ML54b, ML71, ML106, ML157a

Metadata quorum and stream availability are separate

Both regions dark: no meta leader and no create, yet the hub's own stream kept taking writes. One region dark: the meta group stayed healthy, yet that region's stream took no write. A vote does not carry data, and data does not carry a vote.

Evidence: ML116, ML118, ML120, ML139, ML140

A timed-out publish is not a failed publish

The CLI gives up and prints a timeout. The message may still be stored later. Retry with the same Nats-Msg-Id, so a stored copy is not stored twice.

Evidence: ML140a, ML146a, ML151a

A leader field can be stale

After both regions go dark, the three hub servers stop naming the old leader one at a time, not together. Read every hub monitor, and wait.

Evidence: ML116a

The answers, requirement by requirement

D03-R13

Asks: Does a hub step-down put the meta leader in the hub, every time?

The kept runs say: Yes, in every trial of every kept run (ML26–ML36, verdict ML41), and again after a recovery (ML93, ML111). Restarting a hub server that is not the leader does not move it (ML38). The hub leader can be requested. Nothing in the config pins it there (ML5a).

Evidence: ML1, ML2, ML3, ML4, ML5, ML5a, ML6, ML7, ML8, ML9, ML10, ML11, ML12, ML13, ML14, ML15, ML16, ML17, ML18, ML19, ML19a, ML20, ML21, ML22, ML23, ML24, ML25, ML26, ML27, ML28, ML29, ML30, ML31, ML32, ML33, ML34, ML35, ML36, ML36a, ML36b, ML37, ML38, ML39, ML40, ML40a, ML41, ML93, ML93a, ML111, ML111a

D03-R14

Asks: One region dark, leader in the hub: does the leader stay, and do writes and metadata go on?

The kept runs say: Yes. The hub leader held through the dark window (ML44, ML61), the meta term did not move (ML49a, ML66a), and writes and the metadata probe worked (ML45–ML49, ML62–ML66). Verdicts ML50 and ML67.

Evidence: ML42, ML43, ML44, ML45, ML46, ML47, ML48, ML49, ML49a, ML50, ML59, ML60, ML61, ML62, ML63, ML64, ML65, ML66, ML66a, ML67

D03-R15

Asks: One region dark, leader in that region: who wins, and how long does it take?

The kept runs say: A new leader is elected outside the dark region, and writes and metadata go on (ML78–ML83, ML96–ML101). Who wins and how long it took are notes, because nothing promises either (ML78a, ML96a). The winner is not always a hub server.

Evidence: ML76, ML77, ML78, ML78a, ML79, ML80, ML81, ML82, ML83, ML83a, ML84, ML94, ML95, ML96, ML96a, ML97, ML98, ML99, ML100, ML101, ML101a, ML102

D03-R16

Asks: When the region returns: does the leader stay, does the term stay, is the region current? Recovery and stability are reported apart.

The kept runs say: Recovery was met in every valid return round: all peers current, one leader, every message back, writes and metadata working. Stability was not: in some rounds the leader moved (R+3), or the same server came back in a higher term (R+3b). The cross-run table below names each round and each run. Why a return disturbs leadership is not proved.

Evidence: ML51, ML52, ML53, ML54, ML54b, ML54a, ML55, ML56, ML57, ML58, ML68, ML69, ML70, ML71, ML71b, ML71a, ML72, ML73, ML74, ML75, ML85, ML86, ML87, ML88, ML88b, ML88a, ML89, ML90, ML91, ML92, ML103, ML104, ML105, ML106, ML106b, ML106a, ML107, ML108, ML109, ML110, ML129, ML130, ML131, ML132, ML132b, ML132a, ML133, ML134, ML135, ML136

D03-R17

Asks: Both regions dark: does the hub lose the meta quorum even though it is healthy?

The kept runs say: Yes. No hub server names a leader (ML116, ML117), and creating a stream fails with 10008 (ML120, ML120a). But ODOMETER_ARB still takes writes, because its own three replicas are all live in arb (ML118, ML119). With one region back, quorum, a leader, writes and metadata return (ML122–ML128).

Evidence: ML112, ML113, ML114, ML115, ML116, ML116a, ML117, ML118, ML119, ML120, ML120a, ML121, ML122, ML123, ML123a, ML124, ML125, ML126, ML127, ML128

D03-R18

Asks: One region dark: does only that region's stream lose writes?

The kept runs say: Yes. A write to the dark region's stream is not acknowledged (ML140, ML151), while the meta leader holds and the other two streams and the metadata probe keep working (ML139, ML141–ML144, ML150, ML152–ML155). A timed-out publish has an unknown outcome: retry it with the same Nats-Msg-Id (ML140a, ML146a).

Evidence: ML137, ML138, ML139, ML140, ML140a, ML141, ML142, ML143, ML144, ML145, ML146, ML146a, ML147, ML148, ML149, ML150, ML151, ML151a, ML152, ML153, ML154, ML155, ML156, ML157, ML157a, ML158

Limits

  • kill -STOP is not a WAN cut. Each dark region is a clean, total stop. A real partition, with both sides running, is not measured.
  • One machine, loopback only. Every timing is a loopback timing. It says nothing about WAN latency.
  • Few rounds. Each kept run has five return rounds. The counts below are counts of named rounds, not rates.
  • Causes are not proved. Why a return can move the leader, or raise the term with the same leader, is not known. Do not write a cause down.
  • Not in these rows. One unacknowledged write that was stored later was seen in a step-6 part run whose rows were not kept. It is recorded in exercises/EXERCISE_OBSERVATIONS.md, not here.
  • Hand runs are not here. The terminal runs of EXERCISE-10-TERMINAL-STEPS.md are in exercises/EXERCISE_OBSERVATIONS.md.
